title: Shine, Mighty God, on Britain Shine
description: Shine, Mighty God, on Britain Shine in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 67, headed “The nation's prosperity and the church's increase”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Shine, might-y God, on Bri-tain shine With beams of heav-enly grace; Re-veal thy power thro' all our coasts, And shew thy smil-ing face.

lines: Shine, mighty God, on Britain shine
Reveal thy power thro' all our coasts,
And like a wall of guardian fire
When shall thy Name, from shore to shore,
And distant nations know and love
Sing to the Lord, ye distant lands,
While British tongues exalt his praise,
He the great Lord, the sovereign Judge,
Wisely commands the worlds he made
Earth shall obey her Maker's will,
Our God will crown his chosen isle

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
